2015 Q1.gq: Operationally, you'll see on page two of the first quarter earnings supplement, our North America onshore production guidance is unchanged and is expected to be relatively flat compared to 2014.
2015 Q1.bq: Despite these activity reductions, our first quarter North American production averaged 307,000 BOEs per day and exceeded our guidance range of 300,000 BOEs per day to 305,000 BOEs per day.

2015 Q2.bq: During the second quarter, onshore North American production averaged 317,000 BOEs per day and once again came in ahead of our expectations.

2015 Q3.gq: And it's going to have very minimal impact; we're still in a position to raise guidance on our North American position.

2016 Q1.bq: As noted in this morning's press release, companywide, pro forma production of 479,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day was at the high end of our quarterly guidance range of 470,000 BOEs to 480,000 BOEs per day.

2016 Q2.gq: Third, production volumes continue to hold up well and track in line with the increased guidance range we provided last quarter.

2017 Q1.gq: For all other expense items, our first quarter and full year results are generally on track; and thus, our full-year 2017 guidance is unchanged.

2017 Q3.gq: So, our updated fourth quarter production guidance is unchanged.

2017 Q4.bq: And U.S. production was at the high end of our guidance range.

2018 Q1.gq: We established a new Permian Basin production record, exceeded U.S. production guidance in the first quarter, and raised our outlook for the remainder of the year.
2018 Q1.bq: As John outlined, our U.S. production exceeded guidance by 4%, while international production was in line with guidance.

2018 Q2.gq: Both of these are above the high end of our prior guidance, which was increased in May.
2018 Q2.bq: This is most evident in our strong second quarter U.S. results, where solid execution and an increasing pace of activity enabled us to exceed guidance by 7,000 BOEs per day.

2018 Q3.gq: Note that cash tax guidance has been increased for the year to reflect higher income levels internationally, primarily as a result of the strong Brent oil prices.
2018 Q3.bq: We beat and raised our production guidance for the third quarter in a row and we outlined a strong 2019 view.

2018 Q4.gq: Comparing what we laid out for 2019 a year ago to our current outlook, our capital program has been reduced, our production outlook has moved to the top half of our previous guidance range, and our Permian basin oil production has been and will continue to be significantly higher.
2018 Q4.bq: When compared to our original 2018 guidance provided last February it was a consistently strong performance on production volumes as US production exceeded our original midpoint guidance by 4% and international production delivered as guided.

2019 Q2.gq: And our guidance for the full-year has been revised downward.
2019 Q2.bq: The second quarter Apache's total adjusted production exceeded guidance with upstream capital spending of just under $600 million.

2019 Q3.gq: In terms of full year 2019 guidance, we are increasing our annual DD&A to $15.25 per BOE for the impacts previously described.

2019 Q4.bq: Moving now to the fourth quarter, oil production in the Permian Basin exceeded guidance and averaged the highest quarterly rate in Apache's history.

2020 Q3.bq: In terms of production, we exceeded our guidance in the U.S. and delivered in-line volumes internationally.

2021 Q1.gq: Looking ahead, the full year guidance we provided in February is unchanged, and we are clearly off to a good start.
2021 Q1.bq: Our total adjusted production exceeded guidance as Permian oil and gas volumes benefited from a faster-than-expected recovery from the February storm impacts.

2021 Q2.bq: Total adjusted production exceeded our guidance in the second quarter, with the US benefiting from better than expected performance throughout our Permian Basin DUC completion program.

2021 Q3.bq: Most of our financial results were in line with or better than guidance this quarter.

2022 Q1.gq: Our full year U.S. production guidance is unchanged at this time, with oil volumes continuing to perform well.

2022 Q2.gq: We increased our guidance for LOE and decreased guidance for G&A to reflect some of the impacts I spoke of previously.

2022 Q3.bq: Most of our financial results in the third quarter were in line or better than guidance.

2022 Q4.bq: U.S. production exceeded guidance on continued strong performance from our Midland and Delaware Basin oil properties.

2023 Q1.bq: APA met or exceeded production guidance in each of our 3 regions.

2023 Q2.gq: In closing, our original full year production guidance is unchanged and we have reduced our 2023 budget capital and operating expense in aggregate by about $250 million.
2023 Q2.bq: Total adjusted oil production of 154,000 barrels per day exceeded our guidance by 4,000 barrels per day, driven mostly by the US.

2023 Q4.bq: In the fourth quarter, our Cheniere gas sales contract contributed free cash flow and pretax net income of $74 million, which was below guidance, as LNG margins over Houston Ship Channel narrowed through the quarter.

2024 Q2.gq: Accordingly, we are raising our full year estimate of income from third-party oil and gas purchased and sold by $120 million to around $350 million.

2024 Q3.gq: Accordingly, with the persistence of weak pricing into the fourth quarter, we are raising our full year estimate to $500 million.

2025 Q1.bq: Also in Egypt, gas development is going very well, and increasing production volumes have led to an average realized gas price of $3.19 in the quarter, exceeding our guidance of $3.15.

2025 Q4.bq: In Egypt, gross gas production of 501 million cubic feet per day was below guidance due to unplanned temporary pipeline disruptions late in the quarter.

2026 Q1.gq: On decommissioning, we raised guidance on decommissioning spend this year by $20 million.
2026 Q1.bq: In the Permian, operational efficiencies and improved uptime drove oil production above guidance, while gas volumes were curtailed due to weak Waha pricing.
